title: The “you” points to the Prophet; Shia exegetes demur

points.label: The Prophet frowns
points.text: Aisha’s report (al-Tirmidhi) says it came down about the blind **Ibn Umm Maktum**, whom the Prophet turned from while speaking with a revered idolater. Sayyid Qutb reads it as a **reproof of the Prophet**.

points.label: An Umayyad man frowns
points.text: A report from **Imam Jaʿfar al-Sadiq**, approved by **al-Sharif al-Murtada**, names an Umayyad man. Frowning at a poor believer, they argue, clashes with **“a great character”** (68:4).
points.who: al-Murtada; report from al-Sadiq; Shia commentaries

points.label: What the grammar shows
points.text: Verses 1–2 say “he”; from verse 3 the text says **“you”**. **Abdel Haleem** calls this a deliberate shift (**iltifāt**): a reproach to the Prophet that begins by talking about him.
points.who: M. A. S. Abdel Haleem on iltifāt

bottom_text: No consensus. The wording leans to the Prophet, since from verse 3 it says “you”. The Umayyad reading rests on a report and on 68:4, and must explain who the “you” is.
source_label: al-Tirmidhi 3331 · Shia commentary on Surah 80 · Abdel Haleem, “Grammatical shift”
